source: Dionysii Cartusiani Opera Omnia, t. X (Montreuil)

1.title: Visionis Abdiæ prophetæ litteralis expositio: Visio Abdiæ. Hæc dicit Dominus ad Edom.
1.title_en: Literal exposition of the vision of Abdias the prophet: The vision of Abdias. Thus saith the Lord God to Edom.

paras.t: Præmittit Abdias hic titulum duo verba continentem, dicendo: Visio Abdiæ, id est, prophetica revelatio, intellectualisque visio ostensa seu facta Abdiæ, est quæ consequenter describitur, scilicet: Hæc dicit Dominus Deus ad Edom, id est, ad Idumæos pertinent quæ sequuntur. Non enim ad eos Deus locutus est ista immediate per Prophetam, ita quod ipsi verba hæc audierunt; sed de eis, et ad eos, quamvis absentes, loquitur per Abdiam. Auditum, id est prophetalem revelationem, et sermonem internum ministerio angeli subministratum, Idumæorumque populum concernentem, audivimus, præsertim auribus cordis, angelis sanctis in nobis loquentibus, a Domino, tanquam a principali illuminatore, qui per angelos aperit et informat animos Prophetarum. Ait autem pluraliter, Audivimus, quia de ista materia factæ sunt revelationes multis Prophetis: imo pene omnia quæ in visione Abdiæ scribuntur, in Jeremia loco quodam habentur. In Ezechiele quoque, et in Malachia, itemque in Isaia de punitione Idumæorum fit sermo. Et hoc sciendum, quod sicut frater Jacob trinomius fuit, quoniam dictus est Esau, et Edom ob corporis sui ruborem. Edom enim interpretatur sanguineus. In Genesi autem legitur Edom vocatus propter lenticulam, de qua dixit ad Jacob: Da mihi de coctione hac rufa. Tertio appellatus est Seir, id est pilosus, quia in modum pellis hispidus fuit. Simili modo posteri ejus, seu populus de ejus semine propagatus, tribus his vocatur nominibus, scilicet Edom, Seir, et Esau, sicut posteri Jacob frequenter nomine Jacob et Israel designantur.
paras.en: Abdias here sets first a title containing two phrases, saying: [[1:1|The vision of Obadiah|Visio Abdiæ]] [the Douay-Rheims text in the app has the Hebrew form of the name; Challoner prints *Abdias*], that is, the prophetic revelation and intellectual vision shown or made to Abdias, is what is described next, namely: [[1:1|Thus saith the Lord God to Edom|Hæc dicit Dominus Deus ad Edom]], that is, what follows concerns the Idumeans. For God did not say these things to them directly through the Prophet, so that they themselves heard these words; but He speaks of them, and to them, though they are absent, through Abdias. [[1:1|We have heard a rumour|Auditum audivimus]] [Latin *auditum audivimus*, literally "we have heard a hearing"], that is, a prophetic revelation and an inward word supplied by the ministry of an angel and concerning the people of the Idumeans, we have heard, chiefly with the ears of the heart, the holy angels speaking within us, [[1:1|from the Lord|a Domino]], as from the principal enlightener, who opens and instructs the minds of the Prophets through the angels. He says *we have heard* in the plural because revelations on this matter were made to many Prophets: indeed nearly everything written in the vision of Abdias is found in one place in Jeremias[[Jer 49:7||]] [the margin gives Jer. xlix, 7–22]. In Ezechiel also[[Ezech 35:1||]] [the margin gives Ezech. xxxv, the whole chapter], and in Malachias[[Mal 1:2||]] [the margin gives Malach. i, 2–4], and likewise in Isaias[[Is 34:5||]][[Is 34:6||]], there is speech of the punishment of the Idumeans. And this is to be known, that the brother of Jacob had three names, since he was called Esau, and Edom for the redness of his body; for *Edom* is interpreted "bloody". But in Genesis we read that he was called Edom on account of the lentil pottage, of which he said to Jacob: [[Gen 25:30|Give me of this red pottage|Da mihi de coctione hac rufa]]. Thirdly he was called Seir, that is, "hairy", because he was rough like a skin[[Gen 25:25||]] [the margin gives "Ibid. 25", that is, Gen. xxv, 25]. In the same way his descendants, the people sprung from his seed, are called by these three names, namely Edom, Seir and Esau, just as the descendants of Jacob are often designated by the names Jacob and Israel.

paras.t: Et legatum ad gentes misit. Per hunc legatum Hieronymus intelligit Jesum Christum mediatorem Dei ac hominum, de quo ait Aggæus: Veniet Desideratus cunctis gentibus. Et ne putemus hoc mystice dictum, Glossa apertius protestatur: Legatus est homo Christus Jesus, qui mittitur ad Nabuchodonosor et exercitum ejus, ut veniant ad destructionem Idumæorum. Unde et Beda: Legatum, inquit, misit Deus ad gentes, id est, Filium suum ac Verbum direxit ad Nabuchodonosor. Sed quomodo intelligenda sunt hæc, quum Filius tempore illo nondum fuerat incarnatus, et secundum divinam naturam suam non est inferior Patre? Et respondendum, quod duplex est missio Filii Dei. Una spiritualis ac invisibilis, quæ competit ei secundum divinitatem, ut mitti dicatur a Patre ad eos quibus Deo Patre volente et dante aliquid inspiravit. De qua missione Verbi Dei, seu increatæ ac genitæ sapientiæ Patris, scriptum est in Sapientiæ libro: Mitte illam de cœlis sanctis tuis, et a sede magnitudinis tuæ. Alia autem est missio ejus visibilis et humana, quæ convenit ei ratione naturæ assumptæ. — Denique quidam per legatum istum, intelligunt divinum instinctum, qui excitavit inimicos Idumæorum ad præliandum contra eos. Potest quoque per legatum istum intelligi angelus Dei, vel bonus vel malus. In quantum enim Idumæi per sua facinora meruerunt hostibus tradi, et in quantum Deus præordinavit eos a Chaldæis vastari, sic angelus bonus instigavit gentem Chaldaicam contra Edom. In quantum vero Chaldæi fecerunt hoc mala intentione, crudelique animo, sic angelus malus provocavit eos adversus Idumæos. Vel certe legatus fuit ipse Nabuchodonosor, quem Deus per Jeremiam nominat servum suum: qui, Deo volente, gentibus sibi subjectis præcepit aggredi Idumæos.
paras.en: [[1:1|and he hath sent an ambassador to the nations|Et legatum ad gentes misit]]. By this ambassador Jerome understands Jesus Christ, the mediator of God and men, of whom Aggeus says: [[Agg 2:8|THE DESIRED OF ALL NATIONS SHALL COME|Veniet Desideratus cunctis gentibus]]. And lest we think this is said mystically, the Gloss declares it more plainly: The ambassador is the man Christ Jesus, who is sent to Nabuchodonosor and his army, that they may come to destroy the Idumeans. Hence Bede also says: God sent an ambassador to the nations, that is, He directed His Son and Word to Nabuchodonosor. But how are these things to be understood, since at that time the Son had not yet become incarnate, and according to His divine nature He is not inferior to the Father? The answer is that the sending [Latin *missio*, the theological term for the "mission" of a divine Person] of the Son of God is twofold. One is spiritual and invisible, which belongs to Him according to His divinity, so that He is said to be sent by the Father to those whom He has inspired with something, God the Father willing and giving it. Of this mission of the Word of God, that is, of the uncreated and begotten wisdom of the Father, it is written in the book of Wisdom: [[Wis 9:10|Send her out of thy holy heaven, and from the throne of thy majesty|Mitte illam de cœlis sanctis tuis, et a sede magnitudinis tuæ]]. The other is His visible and human mission, which belongs to Him by reason of the nature He assumed. — Lastly, some understand by this ambassador a divine prompting, which stirred up the enemies of the Idumeans to fight against them. By this ambassador an angel of God may also be understood, either good or evil. For inasmuch as the Idumeans by their crimes deserved to be handed over to their enemies, and inasmuch as God foreordained that they should be laid waste by the Chaldeans, in that respect a good angel urged the Chaldean nation against Edom. But inasmuch as the Chaldeans did this with an evil intention and a cruel mind, in that respect an evil angel provoked them against the Idumeans. Or else the ambassador was Nabuchodonosor himself, whom God through Jeremias calls His servant[[Jer 25:9||]]: who, by God's will, commanded the nations subject to him to attack the Idumeans.

paras.t: Præfatus ergo legatus quocumque modo intelligatur, dixit per inspirationem occultam, vel externam allocutionem: Surgite, id est, ad præliandum vos præparate, et consurgamus adversus eum, id est contra populum Edom seu Idumæorum, in prælium. Quasi dicat: Ne timeatis, quia adsistam vobis, et ero in acie. Vel verba ista dicuntur ex persona gentium, ad designandum confœderationem earum contra Edom, ita quod se cohortantur ad prælium.
paras.en: So the aforesaid ambassador, in whichever way he is understood, said, by a hidden inspiration or by outward address: [[1:1|Arise|Surgite]], that is, make yourselves ready to fight, [[1:1|and let us rise up|et consurgamus]] [[1:1|against him|adversus eum]], that is, against the people of Edom or of the Idumeans, [[1:1|to battle|in prælium]]. As if to say: Do not fear, for I will stand by you and be in the battle line. Or these words are said in the person of the nations, to signify their league against Edom, so that they urge one another to battle.

paras.t: Deinde Dominus ait ad populum Idumæorum: Ecce parvulum, id est numero modicum, dedi te in gentibus, id est inter gentes in circuitu tuo commorantes, ita quod nationes aliæ multitudine et potestate te excedunt. Ideo subditur: contemptibilis tu es valde, id est vilior et impotentior aliis. Verumtamen in libro Numerorum habetur, quod rex Edom cum infinita multitudine egressus est obviam filiis Israel, quando petierunt proficisci per terram illius. Unde non videtur certum, quod Idumæi erant numero pauciores aliis gentibus.
paras.en: Then the Lord says to the people of the Idumeans: [[1:2|Behold I have made thee small|Ecce parvulum]] [Latin *parvulum*, "very small"], that is, few in number, [[1:2|among the nations|dedi te in gentibus]], that is, among the nations dwelling round about thee, so that other nations surpass thee in numbers and in power. Therefore it is added: [[1:2|thou art exceeding contemptible|contemptibilis tu es valde]], that is, meaner and weaker than the others. And yet in the book of Numbers we read that the king of Edom came out to meet the children of Israel with an infinite multitude[[Num 20:20||]], when they asked to pass through his land. Hence it does not seem certain that the Idumeans were fewer in number than other nations.

paras.t: Ideo alii exponunt hoc modo: Ecce parvulum dedi, id est, dabo te, ita quod tot occidentur de tuis, quod reliqui erunt paucissimi. Sicque more prophetico ponitur præteritum pro futuro. Quo facto, contemptibiles facti sunt Idumæi.
paras.en: Therefore others explain it in this way: [[1:2|Behold I have made thee small|Ecce parvulum dedi]], that is, I will make thee so, in that so many of thine shall be slain that those left shall be very few. And so, in the prophetic manner, the past is put for the future. When this was done, the Idumeans were made contemptible.

paras.t: Superbia cordis tui extulit te, id est, tumenter erexit ultra vires tuas et propriam conditionem, habitantem in scissuris petrarum, id est in cavernis seu speluncis saxorum, ita quod tecta domorum non habes. Terra quippe Idumæorum, secundum Glossam, sub nimio solis calore est sita, idcirco in cavernis petrarum morantur. Alii tamen per cavernas petrarum intelligunt ædificia difficiles accessus habentia. Exaltantem solium tuum, id est regiam vel judiciariam tuam potestatem, in qua nimis confidis. Qui dicis in corde tuo: Quis detrahet me in terram? id est, quæ gens poterit me superare et conculcare? ac si fortior omnibus esses. Hanc elationem Deus retundit, subdendo: Si exaltatus fueris ut aquila, id est, quantumcumque erexeris atque prætuleris te aliis, sicut aquila omnibus avibus altius volat, et si inter sidera posueris nidum tuum, id est, quamvis hoc posses aut faceres; inde detraham te, dicit Dominus, id est, nihilo minus humiliarem et hostibus darem te. Aquila, ut refert Hieronymus, cunctis avibus altius volat; tamque acutissimi visus est, ut quum super mare immobili penna feratur, nec humano visu possit intueri, de tanta sublimitate pisciculos videt natare: qui quum juxta littus fuerint, descendit, raptamque prædam ad littus pertrahit pennis.
paras.en: [[1:3|The pride of thy heart hath lifted thee up|Superbia cordis tui extulit te]], that is, has puffed thee up and raised thee beyond thy strength and thy own condition, [[1:3|who dwellest in the clefts of the rocks|habitantem in scissuris petrarum]], that is, in the caves or grottoes of the rocks, so that thou hast no roofed houses. For the land of the Idumeans, according to the Gloss, lies under an excessive heat of the sun, and therefore they live in caves in the rocks. Others, however, understand by the caves in the rocks buildings hard of access. [[1:3|and settest up thy throne on high|Exaltantem solium tuum]], that is, thy royal or judicial power, in which thou trustest too much. [[1:3|who sayest in thy heart: Who shall bring me down to the ground?|Qui dicis in corde tuo: Quis detrahet me in terram?]] that is, what nation will be able to overcome me and trample me down? as though thou wert stronger than all. God beats down this haughtiness, adding: [[1:4|Though thou be exalted as an eagle|Si exaltatus fueris ut aquila]], that is, however much thou raise thyself up and set thyself above others, as the eagle flies higher than all birds, [[1:4|and though thou set thy nest among the stars|et si inter sidera posueris nidum tuum]], that is, even if thou couldst or didst do this, [[1:4|thence will I bring thee down, saith the Lord|inde detraham te, dicit Dominus]], that is, I would none the less humble thee and give thee to thy enemies. The eagle, as Jerome relates, flies higher than all birds, and is of such keen sight that when it is borne over the sea on motionless wing, so high that human sight cannot make it out, from that great height it sees the little fish swimming; and when they are near the shore it comes down and drags the prey it has seized to the shore with its wings.

paras.t: Deinde prædicitur omnimoda spoliatio Idumæorum. Si fures introissent ad te, o popule Idumææ, si latrones per noctem habitacula tua intrassent, quomodo conticuisses? id est, non tacuisses, si vigilasses, et illos adesse novisses. Nonne furati essent sufficientia sibi? id est, tantum abstulissent, quantum potuissent portare, et cetera reliquissent, vel quædam omnino dimisissent, eo quod non auderent omnia loca, præsertim secretiora, intrare. Sunt enim timidæ tales personæ. Si vindemiatores introissent ad te, id est ad vineam tuam, ut deponerent uvas, numquid saltem racemum reliquissent tibi? id est, imo quosdam racemos inter folia latitantes, vel sibi superfluentes, stare permisissent. Hæc dicuntur, ad insinuandum cupiditatem et crudelitatem Chaldæorum, qui nihil de substantia Idumæorum dimiserunt, sed omnia diripuerunt, sicut subjungitur: Quomodo scrutati sunt Esau? id est, tam populum quam divitias ejus diligentissime quæsierunt, ad occidendum vel deprædandum. Investigaverunt abscondita ejus, id est subterranea tuguria, quibus Idumæi utuntur, vel bona possessa, quæ absconderunt in secretissimis antris aut loculis.
paras.en: Next the utter plundering of the Idumeans is foretold. [[1:5|If thieves had gone in to thee|Si fures introissent ad te]], O people of Idumea, [[1:5|if robbers by night|si latrones per noctem]] had entered thy dwellings, [[1:5|how wouldst thou have held thy peace?|quomodo conticuisses?]] that is, thou wouldst not have kept silent, if thou hadst been awake and known that they were there. [[1:5|would they not have stolen till they had enough?|Nonne furati essent sufficientia sibi?]] that is, they would have taken away as much as they could carry and left the rest, or would have left some things alone altogether, because they would not dare to go into every place, especially the more secret ones; for such persons are fearful. [[1:5|if the grapegatherers had come in to thee|Si vindemiatores introissent ad te]], that is, into thy vineyard, to take down the grapes, [[1:5|would they not have left thee at the least a cluster?|numquid saltem racemum reliquissent tibi?]] that is, yes indeed, they would have let some clusters stand that lay hidden among the leaves or were more than they needed. These things are said to suggest the greed and cruelty of the Chaldeans, who left nothing of the substance of the Idumeans but plundered everything, as is added: [[1:6|How have they searched Esau|Quomodo scrutati sunt Esau?]] that is, they sought out both his people and his riches most diligently, to kill or to plunder. [[1:6|how have they sought out his hidden things?|Investigaverunt abscondita ejus]], that is, the underground huts which the Idumeans use, or the goods they possessed, which they hid in the most secret caves or chests.

paras.t: Usque ad terminos emiserunt te, id est, de propriis te finibus ejecerunt. Omnes viri fœderis tui, id est, qui tibi paulo ante confœderati erant, ut Moabitæ, Ammonitæ, vel alii, illuserunt tibi, id est deceperunt: quoniam rege atque exercitu Chaldæorum veniente exterriti, non audebant tibi adstare, sed illis se conjunxerunt adversum te. Et in hoc aggravatur calamitas tua, quod ab his impugnaris de quorum amicitia præsumebas. Gravius enim est ab amicis affligi, juxta illud in Psalmo: Quoniam si inimicus meus maledixisset mihi, sustinuissem utique, etc. Propterea scriptum est in libro Job: Qui deridetur ab amico suo, invocabit Dominum, et exaudiet eum. Invaluerunt adversum te viri pacis tuæ, id est, prædicti, cum quibus dudum pacem habebas, una cum Chaldæis te superaverunt, et occidi seu captivari te adjuverunt. Qui comedunt tecum panem, ponent insidias subter te, id est, qui erant commensales tui, jungent se adversariis tuis, dabuntque eis consilium quomodo facilius capiaris ac decipiaris. Hoc nempe fecerunt partim timore, et partim ut per hoc favorem Chaldæorum obtinerent. Et quoniam amici et commensales Idumæorum fuerunt, melius noverant modum circumveniendi et obsidendi coarctandique eos. Propter quod posuerunt eis insidias. Omnia hæc a Jeremia describuntur. Non est prudentia in eo, id est, nulla providentia et circumspectio inest populo Edom, qui tam incaute confisus est in infidelibus amicis, nec aliquem modum evadendi invenit.
paras.en: [[1:7|They have sent thee out even to the border|Usque ad terminos emiserunt te]], that is, they have cast thee out of thy own borders. [[1:7|all the men of thy confederacy|Omnes viri fœderis tui]], that is, those who a little before were in league with thee, such as the Moabites, the Ammonites or others, [[1:7|have deceived thee|illuserunt tibi]], that is, have mocked and deceived thee: for, terrified as the king and army of the Chaldeans came on, they dared not stand by thee, but joined themselves to them against thee. And in this thy calamity is made heavier, that thou art attacked by those on whose friendship thou didst rely. For it is more grievous to be afflicted by friends, according to that saying in the Psalm: [[Ps 54:13|For if my enemy had reviled me, I would verily have borne with it|Quoniam si inimicus meus maledixisset mihi, sustinuissem utique]], etc. Therefore it is written in the book of Job: [[Job 12:4|He that is mocked by his friends|Qui deridetur ab amico suo]], [[Job 12:4|shall call upon God and he will hear him|invocabit Dominum, et exaudiet eum]]. [[1:7|the men of thy peace have prevailed against thee|Invaluerunt adversum te viri pacis tuæ]], that is, the aforesaid, with whom thou hadst long been at peace, have overcome thee together with the Chaldeans, and have helped to have thee slain or taken captive. [[1:7|they that eat with thee|Qui comedunt tecum]] bread [the Douay-Rheims follows the Vulgate, which lacks *panem*, "bread"], [[1:7|shall lay snares under thee|ponent insidias subter te]], that is, those who were thy table-companions will join themselves to thy adversaries, and will give them counsel how thou mayest more easily be taken and deceived. This they did partly out of fear, and partly to win the favour of the Chaldeans by it. And since they had been friends and table-companions of the Idumeans, they knew better the way to get round them, besiege them and hem them in; for which reason they laid snares for them. All these things are described by Jeremias[[Jer 49:7||]] [the margin gives Jer. xlix, 7–22]. [[1:7|there is no wisdom in him|Non est prudentia in eo]], that is, there is no foresight or circumspection in the people of Edom, who trusted so incautiously in faithless friends, and found no way of escape.

paras.t: Numquid non in die illa, id est tempore vastitatis Idumæorum, dicit Dominus, perdam sapientes de Idumæa, id est, sapientes hujus terræ ostendam fuisse insipientes, et sapientiam eorum esse stultitiam, et prudentiam perdam de monte Esau, id est de habitantibus in terra filiorum Esau montuosa? Non quod populus iste habuerit veram sapientiam atque prudentiam, sed quia putabant se prudentes ac sapientes, intenti divinationibus, auguriis ceterisque superstitionibus. Quorum stultitia innotuit, dum imminentia pericula nec prænoscere neque effugere potuerunt. Et timebunt, o Edom, fortes tui a meridie, id est ad meridianam terræ tuæ partem manentes, quando per illam partem adversarii terram tuam ingressi sunt, ut intereat vir de monte Esau, id est, timorem illorum consequetur occisio virorum habitantium in locis montanis, in quibus Esau et posteri ejus habitaverunt. Quoniam enim territi erant robusti Idumææ, non potuerunt resistere: quoniam excessivus timor actum rationis ac fortitudinis impedit. Propter quod scriptum est: Pavor ejus non me terreat; neque enim possum metuens respondere. Denique fortissimus Judas Machabæus, quando confractus est corde, occisus est.
paras.en: [[1:8|Shall not I in that day|Numquid non in die illa]], that is, in the time of the laying waste of the Idumeans, [[1:8|saith the Lord, destroy the wise out of Edom|dicit Dominus, perdam sapientes de Idumæa]], that is, I will show that the wise of this land were unwise, and that their wisdom is folly, [[1:8|and understanding|et prudentiam]] will I destroy [[1:8|out of the mount of Esau?|de monte Esau]], that is, out of those who dwell in the mountainous land of the children of Esau. Not that this people had true wisdom and understanding, but because they thought themselves prudent and wise, given as they were to divinations, auguries and other superstitions. Their folly became known when they could neither foresee nor escape the dangers hanging over them. And [[1:9|shall be afraid|Et timebunt]], O Edom, [[1:9|thy valiant men of the south|fortes tui a meridie]], that is, those living in the southern part of thy land, when the enemy entered thy land through that part, [[1:9|that man may be cut off from the mount of Esau|ut intereat vir de monte Esau]], that is, their fear will be followed by the slaughter of the men living in the mountain places where Esau and his descendants dwelt. For since the strong men of Idumea were terrified, they could not resist: for excessive fear hinders the act of reason and of fortitude. For which reason it is written: [[Job 9:34|let not his fear terrify me|Pavor ejus non me terreat]]; [[Job 9:35|for I cannot answer while I am in fear|neque enim possum metuens respondere]]. And lastly the most valiant Judas Machabeus, when [[1 Mach 9:7|his heart was cast down|confractus est corde]], was slain.

paras.t: Propter interfectionem, et propter iniquitatem in fratrem tuum Jacob, id est, quoniam occidisti Judæos, et persecutus es eos qui sunt fratres tui, quia tu et illi de duobus fratribus, scilicet Jacob et Esau, descendistis, operiet te confusio, id est, ex omni parte confunderis et destrueris, et peribis in æternum, id est æterna captivitate, videlicet absque regni reparatione, quemadmodum in Jeremiæ prophetia habetur: Per memetipsum juravi, dicit Dominus, quod in solitudinem, et in opprobrium, et in desertum, et in maledictionem erit Bosra, et omnes civitates ejus erunt in solitudines sempiternas. Quemadmodum autem Esau odivit et persecutus est Jacob pro benedictione quam sibi præripuit; sic Idumæi prosperitati filiorum Israel jugiter inviderunt ac restiterunt, plura mala inferendo eisdem. De hoc quoque dictum est supra ab Amos: Super tribus sceleribus Edom, et super quatuor non convertam eum, eo quod persecutus sit in gladio fratrem suum, et violaverit misericordiam suam, et tenuerit ultra furorem suum. Unde jam subditur:
paras.en: [[1:10|For the slaughter, and for the iniquity against thy brother Jacob|Propter interfectionem, et propter iniquitatem in fratrem tuum Jacob]], that is, because thou hast slain the Jews and persecuted those who are thy brethren, since thou and they are descended from two brothers, namely Jacob and Esau, [[1:10|confusion shall cover thee|operiet te confusio]], that is, thou shalt be confounded and destroyed on every side, [[1:10|and thou shalt perish for ever|et peribis in æternum]], that is, by an everlasting captivity, namely without restoration of the kingdom, as is found in the prophecy of Jeremias: [[Jer 49:13|I have sworn by myself, saith the Lord, that Bosra shall become a desolation, and a reproach, and a desert, and a curse: and all her cities shall be everlasting wastes|Per memetipsum juravi, dicit Dominus, quod in solitudinem, et in opprobrium, et in desertum, et in maledictionem erit Bosra, et omnes civitates ejus erunt in solitudines sempiternas]]. And as Esau hated and persecuted Jacob for the blessing which he snatched from him[[Gen 27:41||]], so the Idumeans continually envied and opposed the prosperity of the children of Israel, inflicting many evils upon them. Of this too it was said above by Amos: [[Amos 1:11|For three crimes of Edom, and for four I will not convert him: because he hath pursued his brother with the sword|Super tribus sceleribus Edom, et super quatuor non convertam eum, eo quod persecutus sit in gladio fratrem suum]], and hath violated his own compassion [the Douay-Rheims text in the app lacks these words, *et violaverit misericordiam ejus*; Challoner has "and hath cast off all pity"], [[Amos 1:11|and hath carried on his fury|et tenuerit ultra furorem suum]]. Hence it is now added:

paras.t: In die quum stares adversus eum, id est populum Judæorum, quando capiebant alieni, id est Chaldæi, exercitum ejus, videlicet Joakim regem Juda, et multos cum eo, inter quos fuerunt Daniel atque Ezechiel, et extranei, id est Chaldæi jam dicti, ingrediebantur portas ejus, puta Jerusalem, aliarumque civitatum Judæ, et super Jerusalem, id est spolia civitatis, mittebant sortem quis quid tolleret; tu quoque eras quasi unus ex eis, id est, in scelere similis fuisti Chaldæis, partem prædæ quæ tibi sorte exiit, diripiendo. Quasi, hoc loco dicit veritatem, non similitudinem tantum.
paras.en: [[1:11|In the day when thou stoodest against him|In die quum stares adversus eum]], that is, against the people of the Jews, [[1:11|when strangers carried away|quando capiebant alieni]], that is, the Chaldeans, [[1:11|his army captive|exercitum ejus]], namely Joakim king of Juda [Latin *Joakim*; that is, Joachin or Jechonias, carried off with Daniel and Ezechiel], and many with him, among whom were Daniel and Ezechiel, [[1:11|and foreigners|et extranei]], that is, the Chaldeans already mentioned, [[1:11|entered into his gates|ingrediebantur portas ejus]], that is, of Jerusalem and the other cities of Juda, [[1:11|and cast lots upon Jerusalem|et super Jerusalem mittebant sortem]], that is, upon the spoils of the city, to see who should take what: [[1:11|thou also wast as one of them|tu quoque eras quasi unus ex eis]], that is, in crime thou wast like the Chaldeans, plundering the share of the booty that fell to thee by lot. *As* here expresses the truth, not a likeness only.

paras.t: Et non despicies in die fratris tui, id est, quum populo Judæorum præter prædictam, captivitas alia evenerit, non despicies eum in die peregrinationis ejus, id est, quum ad alienam terram transferetur captivus; et non lætaberis super filios Juda, id est, de vastitate et pressuris duarum tribuum non gaudebis, in die perditionis, id est captivitatis eorum; et non magnificabis os tuum, id est, non lato ore ridebis, nec superba loqueris, in die angustiæ Judæorum.
paras.en: [[1:12|But thou shalt not look on in the day of thy brother|Et non despicies in die fratris tui]] [Latin *despicies*, "thou shalt look down on", that is, with scorn], that is, when another captivity besides the one just mentioned befalls the people of the Jews, thou shalt not look down on him [[1:12|in the day of his leaving his country|in die peregrinationis ejus]], that is, when he is carried captive to a foreign land; [[1:12|and thou shalt not rejoice over the children of Juda|et non lætaberis super filios Juda]], that is, thou shalt not be glad at the laying waste and the afflictions of the two tribes, [[1:12|in the day of their destruction|in die perditionis]], that is, of their captivity; [[1:12|and thou shalt not magnify thy mouth|et non magnificabis os tuum]], that is, thou shalt not laugh with open mouth nor speak proud things, [[1:12|in the day of distress|in die angustiæ]] of the Jews.

paras.t: Neque ingredieris portam populi mei, id est urbem Jerusalem, in die ruinæ eorum, id est, quando coram adversariis suis cadent Judæi, quemadmodum factum est tempore Sedeciæ regis Juda. Causa vero istorum est, quia et ipsi Idumæi interim a Chaldæis oppressi sunt, et propriam cladem sic deplorabant, quod de negotio aliorum non intromiserunt se quemadmodum ante. Aliqui etiam expositores affirmant, quod ante destructionem Jerusalem et templi combustionem, Idumæi a Chaldæis capti fuerunt. Quod non videtur omnifarie certum, quum in Psalmo dicatur: Memor esto, Domine, filiorum Edom in die Jerusalem, qui dicunt, Exinanite, exinanite, usque ad fundamentum in ea. Neque despicies et tu populum Juda in malis, id est afflictionibus ejus, in die vastitatis illius, id est tempore suæ persecutionis. Et non emitteris, id est, de terra tua non destinaberis, adversum exercitum ejus, id est contra populum Judæorum, in die vastitatis illius.
paras.en: [[1:13|Neither shalt thou enter into the gate of my people|Neque ingredieris portam populi mei]], that is, the city of Jerusalem, [[1:13|in the day of their ruin|in die ruinæ eorum]], that is, when the Jews fall before their adversaries, as happened in the time of Sedecias king of Juda[[4 Kings 25:1||]] [the margin gives IV Reg. xxv, the whole chapter]. And the reason for these things is that the Idumeans themselves were meanwhile oppressed by the Chaldeans, and so lamented their own disaster that they did not meddle in the business of others as before. Some expositors also affirm that the Idumeans were taken by the Chaldeans before the destruction of Jerusalem and the burning of the temple. This does not seem altogether certain, since it is said in the Psalm: [[Ps 136:7|Remember, O Lord, the children of Edom, in the day of Jerusalem: Who say: Rase it, rase it, even to the foundation thereof|Memor esto, Domine, filiorum Edom in die Jerusalem, qui dicunt, Exinanite, exinanite, usque ad fundamentum in ea]]. [[1:13|neither shalt thou also look on|Neque despicies et tu]] the people of Juda [[1:13|in his evils|in malis]], that is, in his afflictions, [[1:13|in the day of his calamity|in die vastitatis illius]], that is, in the time of his persecution. [[1:13|and thou shalt not be sent out|Et non emitteris]], that is, thou shalt not be dispatched from thy land, [[1:13|against his army|adversum exercitum ejus]], that is, against the people of the Jews, [[1:13|in the day of his desolation|in die vastitatis illius]] [the Latin has *in die vastitatis illius* both times; the Douay-Rheims varies it as "calamity" and "desolation"].

paras.t: Neque stabis in exitibus viarum, id est in abditis locis ubi declinatur a solita via, per quæ fugientes solent excurrere, ut interficias eos qui fugerint, id est Judæos fugientes a facie Chaldæorum, vel aliorum, a quibus post reditum a Babylone vexati sunt; et non concludes reliquos ejus, id est, non valentes effugere non claudes in carcere, non comprehendes neque ligabis, in die tribulationis Judæorum. Hæc ergo non facies de cetero, sicut fecisti frequenter.
paras.en: [[1:14|Neither shalt thou stand in the crossways|Neque stabis in exitibus]] [Latin *in exitibus*, literally "in the outlets"] of the roads, that is, in hidden places where one turns off from the usual road, through which fugitives commonly run out, [[1:14|to kill them that flee|ut interficias eos qui fugerint]], that is, the Jews fleeing from the face of the Chaldeans, or of others by whom they were harassed after the return from Babylon; [[1:14|and thou shalt not shut up them that remain of him|et non concludes reliquos ejus]], that is, thou shalt not shut up in prison those unable to escape, nor seize nor bind them, [[1:14|in the day of tribulation|in die tribulationis]] of the Jews. These things, then, thou shalt not do henceforth, as thou hast often done.

paras.t: Quoniam juxta est dies Domini, id est, tempus ultionis divinæ imminet, super omnes gentes, id est super universas nationes terrarum climatis tui, inter quas et tu una es. Hoc, secundum Hieronymum, intelligendum est de vastitate et dejectione gentium, quas primo ab Assyriis, deinde a Chaldæis perpessæ sunt. Assyrii enim et Chaldæi universas regiones illas demoliti sunt, sicut in diversis patet historiis. Sicut fecisti Judæis, o Edom, fiet tibi a Chaldæis; retributionem tuam convertet in caput tuum, id est, pœnam quam meruisti, Dominus tibi infligit per Chaldæos. Quocirca asserit Glossa: Sicut cum Babyloniis lætabaris de destructione Jerusalem ubi erat templum et altare; ita lætabuntur de effusione sanguinis tui gentes illæ quas tecum habebat Babylonius in præsidio, id est, quæ tecum adjuverunt Chaldæos contra Jerusalem. Ex quo sequi videtur, quod Idumæi interfuerunt destructioni Jerusalem tempore Nabuchodonosor, et postea puniti fuerunt. Quod utique Scripturis canonicis amplius consonat: imo Isaias diversis in locis, et Ezechiel, Jeremias quoque, hoc in suis libris insinuant.
paras.en: [[1:15|For the day of the Lord is at hand|Quoniam juxta est dies Domini]], that is, the time of God's vengeance is imminent, [[1:15|upon all nations|super omnes gentes]], that is, upon all the nations of thy region of the earth, among which thou too art one. According to Jerome, this is to be understood of the laying waste and overthrow of the nations which they suffered first from the Assyrians, then from the Chaldeans. For the Assyrians and Chaldeans destroyed all those regions, as is plain from various histories. [[1:15|as thou hast done|Sicut fecisti]] to the Jews, O Edom, [[1:15|so shall it be done to thee|fiet tibi]] by the Chaldeans; [[1:15|he will turn thy reward upon thy own head|retributionem tuam convertet in caput tuum]], that is, the Lord inflicts on thee through the Chaldeans the punishment thou hast deserved. Wherefore the Gloss says: As thou didst rejoice with the Babylonians at the destruction of Jerusalem, where the temple and the altar were, so those nations which the Babylonian had with thee as auxiliaries [in præsidio: literally in garrison] shall rejoice at the shedding of thy blood; that is, those which helped the Chaldeans against Jerusalem together with thee. From this it seems to follow that the Idumeans took part in the destruction of Jerusalem in the time of Nabuchodonosor, and were punished afterwards. And this certainly agrees better with the canonical Scriptures; indeed Isaias in various places[[Is 34:1||]], and Ezechiel[[Ezech 35:1||]], and Jeremias also[[Jer 49:1||]], hint at this in their books.

paras.t: Quomodo enim bibisti super montem sanctum meum, id est, de Jerusalem et templi in monte Sion siti destructione gavisus et epulatus es, atque de spoliis Judæorum potasti; bibent omnes gentes jugiter, id est, prædictæ nationes Chaldæis junctæ, de tua vastitate gaudebunt et bona tua consument jugiter, quousque in terra tua permanserint, et bibent et absorbebunt, id est, te occident, et tuas divitias devorabunt; et erunt quasi non sint, id est, Idumæi quasi in nihilum redigentur. Vel gentes illæ erunt quasi non sint, quia et ipsæ peribunt. Persæ enim ac Medi destruxerunt Chaldæos cum adjutoribus suis. Macedones vero, seu Græci, Persas ac Medos vicerunt, et Romani Græcos. Vel sic: Quomodo bibisti super montem sanctum meum, id est, quemadmodum calicem vindictæ potasti propter iniquitatem tuam factam contra Jerusalem et templum (de quo calice habetur in Psalmo: Calix in manu Domini, bibent omnes peccatores terræ), sic et ceteræ gentes bibituræ sunt calicem istum. Unde per Jeremiam loquitur Dominus: Calix aureus Babylon in manu Domini, inebrians omnes gentes. Et absorbebunt, id est, usque ad fæcem bibent hunc calicem.
paras.en: [[1:16|For as you have drunk upon my holy mountain|Quomodo enim bibisti super montem sanctum meum]], that is, thou didst rejoice and feast over the destruction of Jerusalem and of the temple set on Mount Sion, and didst drink of the spoils of the Jews; [[1:16|so all nations shall drink continually|bibent omnes gentes jugiter]], that is, the aforesaid nations joined to the Chaldeans shall rejoice at thy laying waste and consume thy goods continually, as long as they remain in thy land; [[1:16|and they shall drink, and sup up|et bibent et absorbebunt]], that is, they shall slay thee and devour thy riches; [[1:16|and they shall be as though they were not|et erunt quasi non sint]], that is, the Idumeans shall be brought as it were to nothing. Or: those nations shall be as though they were not, because they too shall perish. For the Persians and Medes destroyed the Chaldeans with their helpers; the Macedonians, or Greeks, conquered the Persians and Medes, and the Romans the Greeks. Or thus: [[1:16|as you have drunk upon my holy mountain|Quomodo bibisti super montem sanctum meum]], that is, as thou hast drunk the cup of vengeance for thy iniquity committed against Jerusalem and the temple (of which cup it is said in the Psalm: [[Ps 74:9|in the hand of the Lord there is a cup|Calix in manu Domini]], [[Ps 74:9|all the sinners of the earth shall drink|bibent omnes peccatores terræ]]), so the other nations too are to drink this cup. Whence the Lord speaks through Jeremias: [[Jer 51:7|Babylon hath been a golden cup in the hand of the Lord, that made all the earth drunk|Calix aureus Babylon in manu Domini, inebrians omnes gentes]] [Denis reads *all the nations* for *all the earth*]. [[1:16|and sup up|Et absorbebunt]], that is, they shall drink this cup to the dregs.

paras.t: Consequenter describitur prosperitas Judæorum. Quæ autem sequuntur, difficiliora sunt præcedentibus. Unde duplicem ponam expositionem illorum. Prima est secundum Hieronymum et eum sequentes.
paras.en: Next the prosperity of the Jews is described. What follows is more difficult than what has gone before; so I shall give a twofold exposition of it. The first is according to Jerome and those who follow him.

paras.t: Et in monte Sion erit salvatio, id est, Idumæis et ceteris gentibus modo præfato vastatis, in monte Sion erit salvatio, id est, templum et civitas reædificabuntur in monte quo steterant prius. Una enim pars civitatis erat in monte jam dicto. Vel, In monte isto erit salvatio, id est, reliquiæ Judæorum a manibus Chaldæorum, aliorumque hostium liberatæ, et per gratiam Dei sanctificatæ, venient et consistent in monte Sion, ut templum et urbem restaurent in eo. Et erit sanctus mons Sion, id est ad divinum obsequium deputatus, propter templum in eo constructum, vel propter sanctitatem eorum qui fuerunt et Domino servierunt in ipso, inter quos fuerunt Aggæus, Zacharias, Esdras, Nehemias, Zorobabel, etc. Et possidebit domus Jacob, id est Judæi a Babylonica captivitate reducti, seu posteri filiique eorum, eos qui se possederant, id est nationes in gyro manentes, a quibus ante Babylonicam captivitatem, vel postea, vastabantur. Quod maxime fuit impletum tempore Machabæorum, quemadmodum primo et secundo Machabæorum copiose describitur: ubi triumphi Judæ et fratrum ejus contra Idumæos, Syros, Philistæos ac ceteras nationes feruntur. Scriptum est etiam in Machabæorum libris, quod Judas efficiebatur intolerabilis gentibus, et dilatavit gloriam populo suo, et persecutus est iniquos.
paras.en: [[1:17|And in mount Sion shall be salvation|Et in monte Sion erit salvatio]], that is, when the Idumeans and the other nations have been laid waste in the way just described, there shall be salvation in Mount Sion: that is, the temple and the city shall be rebuilt on the mountain where they had stood before; for one part of the city was on the mountain just named. Or, [[1:17|in mount Sion shall be salvation|In monte isto erit salvatio]] [Denis here says *in this mountain*]: that is, the remnant of the Jews, delivered from the hands of the Chaldeans and of their other enemies and sanctified by the grace of God, shall come and settle on Mount Sion, to restore the temple and the city on it. [[1:17|and it shall be holy|Et erit sanctus]], Mount Sion, that is, set apart for the service of God, because of the temple built on it, or because of the holiness of those who were there and served the Lord in it, among whom were Aggeus, Zacharias, Esdras, Nehemias, Zorobabel, etc.[[1 Esd 5:2||]][[1 Esd 6:1||]][[2 Esd 2:1||]][[Ecclus 49:13||]] [[1:17|and the house of Jacob shall possess|Et possidebit domus Jacob]], that is, the Jews brought back from the Babylonian captivity, or their descendants and sons, [[1:17|those that possessed them|eos qui se possederant]], that is, the nations dwelling round about, by whom they were laid waste before the Babylonian captivity, or afterwards. This was fulfilled above all in the time of the Machabees, as is described at length in the first and second books of Machabees[[1 Mach 5:1||]][[2 Mach 12:1||]], where the triumphs of Judas and his brothers over the Idumeans, Syrians, Philistines and other nations are related. It is written too in the books of Machabees that Judas [[2 Mach 8:5|could not be withstood by the heathens|efficiebatur intolerabilis gentibus]], and [[1 Mach 3:3|he got his people great honour|dilatavit gloriam populo suo]], and [[1 Mach 3:5|he pursued the wicked|persecutus est iniquos]].

paras.t: Et erit domus Jacob, id est duæ tribus, ignis, per proprietatem et similitudinem quoad destructionem hostium, ut patebit; et domus Joseph, id est familia decem tribuum, erit flamma similitudinarie. Dicuntur autem decem tribus, domus Joseph, quoniam primus rex earum erat de tribu Ephraim filii Joseph. Eratque tribus Joseph principalior inter decem, quia et Joseph data sunt primogenita, eo quod Ruben violasset torum proprii genitoris, ut dicitur primo Paralipomenon libro. Et domus Esau, id est populus Idumæus, erit stipula, id est similis stipulæ: quoniam ut stipula ab igne cito consumitur, sic Idumæi a Judæis, secundum quod subditur: Et succendetur, id est, Idumæa igne tribulationis destruetur, in eis, id est a duabus decemque tribubus. Et devorabunt eos, id est, vincent et interficient Idumæos; et non erunt reliquiæ domus Esau, id est, nulli aut pauci Idumæorum effugient. Quamvis autem decem tribus fuerunt translatæ et captæ ante duarum tribuum captivitatem, et post earum liberationem captæ manserunt, et nunc usque permanent captæ; nihilo minus, ut patet ex libris Regum et Paralipomenon, multi de decem tribubus evaserunt manus Assyriorum, et duabus tribubus se junxerunt ante captivitatem Babylonicam et post, qui nunc dicuntur domus Joseph. De quibus Jeremias, Ezechiel et Zacharias prædixerunt, quod constituerent sibi caput unum. Hi ergo ad invicem congregati, demoliti sunt Idumæos. Quia Dominus locutus est.
paras.en: [[1:18|And the house of Jacob shall be|Et erit domus Jacob]], that is, the two tribes, [[1:18|a fire|ignis]], by way of property and likeness as regards the destruction of enemies, as will be plain; [[1:18|and the house of Joseph|et domus Joseph]], that is, the family of the ten tribes, shall be [[1:18|a flame|flamma]] by likeness. Now the ten tribes are called the house of Joseph because their first king was of the tribe of Ephraim, the son of Joseph. And the tribe of Joseph was the chief among the ten, because the birthright too was given to Joseph, since Ruben had defiled his own father's bed[[Gen 35:22||]], as is said in the first book of Paralipomenon[[1 Par 5:1||]]. [[1:18|and the house of Esau|Et domus Esau]], that is, the Idumean people, shall be [[1:18|stubble|erit stipula]], that is, like stubble: for as stubble is quickly consumed by fire, so are the Idumeans by the Jews, according to what is added: [[1:18|and they shall be kindled|Et succendetur]] [Denis reads the singular, *it shall be kindled*], that is, Idumea shall be destroyed by the fire of tribulation, [[1:18|in them|in eis]], that is, by the two tribes and the ten. [[1:18|and shall devour them|Et devorabunt eos]], that is, they shall conquer and slay the Idumeans; [[1:18|and there shall be no remains of the house of Esau|et non erunt reliquiæ domus Esau]], that is, none or few of the Idumeans shall escape. Now although the ten tribes were carried away and taken captive before the captivity of the two tribes, and remained captive after the two were set free, and remain captive to this day, nevertheless, as is plain from the books of Kings and Paralipomenon[[4 Kings 23:22||]][[2 Par 35:17||]][[2 Par 30:5||]] [the margin gives IV Reg. xxii, 22, 23; the passover of Josias, which the Israelites who were left kept with Juda, is at 4 Kings 23:22–23], many of the ten tribes escaped the hands of the Assyrians and joined themselves to the two tribes, before the Babylonian captivity and after; and these are now called the house of Joseph. Of them Jeremias, Ezechiel[[Ezech 34:23||]][[Ezech 37:24||]] and Zacharias foretold that they would set up one head over themselves [the places in Ezechiel speak of *one shepherd*; the words *one head* are those of Osee 1:11]. These, then, gathered together, destroyed the Idumeans. [[1:18|for the Lord hath spoken it|Quia Dominus locutus est]].

paras.t: Et hereditabunt, post reditum a Babylone, hi qui ad austrum sunt, id est Judæi ad partem australem sive meridiem habitantes (ibi enim erat sors Juda, ut scribitur in libro Josue), montem Esau, id est loca montana Idumæorum, quos superaverunt; et qui in campestribus, id est illi qui ex duabus tribubus in locis campestribus morabantur, quorum civitates Hieronymus exprimit, hereditabunt Philistiim, id est terram Philistinorum. De hoc multa habentur in libris Machabæorum. Et possidebunt regionem Ephraim et regionem Samariæ, vel dominando seu prævalendo Samaritanis, aut aliquid de terra eorum obtinendo. Et Benjamin possidebit Galaad, id est, filii Benjamin a captivitate reversi, plagam Arabiæ nomine Galaad obtinebunt. Dilataverunt enim terminos suos circumquaque omnes Judæi jam nominati, quantum valebant.
paras.en: [[1:19|shall inherit|Et hereditabunt]], after the return from Babylon, [[1:19|they that are toward the south|hi qui ad austrum sunt]], that is, the Jews living in the southern part, or the south (for there lay the lot of Juda, as is written in the book of Josue[[Jos 15:1||]][[Jos 15:21||]]), [[1:19|the mount of Esau|montem Esau]], that is, the mountain country of the Idumeans, whom they overcame; [[1:19|and they that are in the plains|et qui in campestribus]], that is, those of the two tribes who lived in the plain country, whose cities Jerome names, shall inherit [[1:19|the Philistines|Philistiim]], that is, the land of the Philistines. Much is found about this in the books of Machabees[[1 Mach 5:1||]][[2 Mach 12:1||]]. [[1:19|and they shall possess the country of Ephraim, and the country of Samaria|Et possidebunt regionem Ephraim et regionem Samariæ]], either by ruling or prevailing over the Samaritans, or by obtaining some of their land. [[1:19|and Benjamin shall possess Galaad|Et Benjamin possidebit Galaad]], that is, the sons of Benjamin returned from captivity shall obtain the tract of Arabia called Galaad. For all the Jews just named widened their borders round about, as far as they were able.

paras.t: Et transmigratio exercitus hujus filiorum Israel, id est Judæi seu filii Israel a Chaldæa reversi, ad quam erant translati, propter quod transmigratio nuncupatur, possidebit omnia loca Chananæorum usque ad Sareptam, id est terras et loca quæ possederunt Chananæi, antequam Deus introduxit filios Israel in terram illam. Sarepta vero est urbs Sidoniorum, in qua vidua pavit Eliam. Et transmigratio Jerusalem quæ in Bosphoro est, id est Judæi de Jerusalem translati in locum qui dicitur Bosphorum: quod est nomen loci in regno Babyloniæ, ut aliqui dicunt; alii vero putant, quod sit nomen loci in quem Adrianus imperator transtulit Judæos; possidebit civitates austri, id est urbes suas sitas, ut dictum est, in plaga australi. Oppida enim ibi destructa reparaverunt.
paras.en: [[1:20|And the captivity of this host of the children of Israel|Et transmigratio exercitus hujus filiorum Israel]], that is, the Jews or children of Israel returned from Chaldea, to which they had been carried away, which is why they are called the captivity [transmigratio: literally the removal, a people carried off to another land], shall possess [[1:20|all the places of the Chanaanites even to Sarepta|omnia loca Chananæorum usque ad Sareptam]], that is, the lands and places which the Chanaanites possessed before God brought the children of Israel into that land. Sarepta is a city of the Sidonians, in which a widow fed Elias[[3 Kings 17:9||]]. [[1:20|and the captivity of Jerusalem that is in Bosphorus|Et transmigratio Jerusalem quæ in Bosphoro est]], that is, the Jews carried away from Jerusalem to the place called Bosphorus: which, as some say, is the name of a place in the kingdom of Babylonia, while others think it is the name of the place to which the emperor Hadrian removed the Jews; [[1:20|shall possess the cities of the south|possidebit civitates austri]], that is, their own cities, situated, as has been said, in the southern tract; for they repaired the towns that had been destroyed there.

paras.t: Et ascendent salvatores, id est Esdras, Zorobabel, Jesus filius Josedec sacerdos magnus, quorum ducatu et ope salvati sunt filii Israel a Babylonica captivitate: unde in libro Judicum dicitur Deus misisse salvatores, qui liberarent Israelem de manu vastantium; in montem Sion: ibi enim frequenter convenerunt; judicare montem Esau, id est Idumæos tanquam subjectos et victos. Et erit Domino regnum, id est, his factis, Judæi servient Deo, non idolis.
paras.en: [[1:21|And saviours shall come up|Et ascendent salvatores]], that is, Esdras, Zorobabel, and Jesus the son of Josedec, the high priest[[1 Esd 2:1||]][[1 Esd 2:2||]][[1 Esd 7:1||]], under whose leadership and by whose help the children of Israel were saved from the Babylonian captivity: whence in the book of Judges God is said to have sent saviours to deliver Israel out of the hand of those who laid them waste[[Judg 2:16||]][[Judg 3:9||]][[Judg 3:15||]]; [[1:21|into mount Sion|in montem Sion]]: for there they often assembled; [[1:21|to judge the mount of Esau|judicare montem Esau]], that is, the Idumeans, as subject and conquered. [[1:21|and the kingdom shall be for the Lord|Et erit Domino regnum]], that is, when these things are done the Jews shall serve God, not idols.

paras.t: Denique, circa prædicta dicit gloriosus et sanctus Hieronymus: Hæc utrum facta sint, Deus viderit. Possunt enim ex parte per annos quingentos a Babylonica captivitate usque ad Christi adventum esse completa. Et iterum ait in fine expositionis hujus Prophetæ: In hoc Propheta, et adolescentuli lusimus, et senes præsumpsimus. Qui veriora melioraque dixerit, in illius sententiam, o Pammachi, transgredere. Exposuit autem Hieronymus hunc Prophetam bis. Primo, in adolescentia sua, secundum tropologicum intellectum. Quam expositionem nominat lusum, quoniam litteralem sensum omisit. Sicut enim in ludo est libera quædam evagatio, ita in tropologica expositione, secundum Hieronymum. Secundo, in senectute sua. Ex quibus Hieronymi verbis constat, quod præinducta expositio non habet certitudinem absolutam: præsertim, quum nec ex Scripturis canonicis, nec ex authenticis historiis queant probari omnia quæ in hujus Prophetæ explanatione sunt dicta, præsertim ab eo loco quo dicitur, Et erit domus Jacob ignis.
paras.en: Lastly, the glorious and holy Jerome says of the foregoing: Whether these things have come to pass, God will see [that is, God knows; Jerome leaves the question open]. For they may have been fulfilled in part during the five hundred years from the Babylonian captivity to the coming of Christ. And again he says at the end of his exposition of this Prophet: On this Prophet we have both played as a youth and presumed as an old man. Whoever has said truer and better things, pass over to his opinion, O Pammachius. Now Jerome expounded this Prophet twice: first in his youth, according to the tropological sense [that is, the figurative or moral sense]; and this exposition he calls play, because he left out the literal sense. For as in play there is a certain free wandering, so is there in tropological exposition, according to Jerome. Secondly, in his old age. From these words of Jerome it is clear that the foregoing exposition has no absolute certainty: especially since not all that has been said in the explanation of this Prophet can be proved either from the canonical Scriptures or from authentic histories, especially from the place where it says, [[1:18|And the house of Jacob shall be a fire|Et erit domus Jacob ignis]].

paras.t: Porro Hebræi intelligunt ista de temporali dominio, quod sibi in adventu Messiæ inaniter repromittunt, ita quod tunc in Judæam reducentur, et omnibus mundi regnis ac gentibus principabuntur. Promissiones enim Prophetarum carnaliter carnales intelligunt. Quidam vero doctores catholici, quantum ad hoc assequuntur Hebræos, quod præinducta exponunt pro tempore Christi.
paras.en: The Hebrews, moreover, understand these things of a temporal dominion which they vainly promise themselves at the coming of the Messias: that they will then be brought back into Judea and rule over all the kingdoms and nations of the world. For, being carnal, they understand the promises of the Prophets carnally. Some Catholic doctors, however, follow the Hebrews in this much, that they expound the foregoing of the time of Christ.

paras.t: Secundum quos iste est sensus: In monte Sion erit salvatio, id est salus et gratia Christi, seu electæ reliquiæ, scilicet primitiva Ecclesia ex Judaismo conversa, quæ in cœnaculo sito in monte Sion Spiritum Sanctum recepit. Et ipsa, recepto Spiritu Sancto, primo orsa est evangelicæ legis doctrinam prædicare in monte Sion, et deinde in aliis locis, quemadmodum Isaias prædixit: De Sion exibit lex, et verbum Domini de Jerusalem. Christus quoque per se ipsum frequenter docuit et miracula maxima fecit in templo. De quo Malachias locutus est: Statim veniet ad templum suum Dominator, quem vos quæritis, et Angelus testamenti, quem vos vultis. Ideo dixit Psalmista: Suscepimus, Deus, misericordiam tuam in medio templi tui. Et erit sanctus: quia tunc sanctissima opera fiebant in monte Sion; et sicut Isaias prænuntiavit, tunc fuit mons domus Domini in vertice montium. Et possidebit domus Jacob, id est sancti Apostoli filii Jacob patriarchæ, eos qui se possederant, id est gentes universas, quæ aliquando populum Israel vexaverunt ac subjecerunt. Hoc intelligendum est de spirituali dominio, non de temporali imperio. Tunc enim constituti sunt Apostoli principes super omnem terram; et dii fortes terræ elevati sunt vehementer.
paras.en: According to them this is the sense: [[1:17|in mount Sion shall be salvation|In monte Sion erit salvatio]], that is, the salvation and grace of Christ, or the chosen remnant, namely the primitive Church converted from Judaism, which received the Holy Ghost in the upper room that stood on Mount Sion[[Acts 2:1||]]. And having received the Holy Ghost, it first began to preach the doctrine of the law of the Gospel on Mount Sion, and afterwards in other places, as Isaias foretold: [[Is 2:3|the law shall come forth from Sion, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem|De Sion exibit lex, et verbum Domini de Jerusalem]]. Christ too often taught in person, and worked the greatest miracles, in the temple[[Luke 19:47||]][[Luke 21:37||]][[John 7:14||]][[John 7:28||]][[Matt 21:14||]]. Of which Malachias spoke: [[Mal 3:1|presently the Lord, whom you seek, and the angel of the testament, whom you desire, shall come to his temple|Statim veniet ad templum suum Dominator, quem vos quæritis, et Angelus testamenti, quem vos vultis]]. Therefore the Psalmist said: [[Ps 47:10|We have received thy mercy, O God, in the midst of thy temple|Suscepimus, Deus, misericordiam tuam in medio templi tui]]. [[1:17|and it shall be holy|Et erit sanctus]]: because then most holy works were done on Mount Sion; and, as Isaias foretold, then was [[Is 2:2|the mountain of the house of the Lord|mons domus Domini]] [[Is 2:2|on the top of mountains|in vertice montium]]. [[1:17|and the house of Jacob shall possess|Et possidebit domus Jacob]], that is, the holy Apostles, sons of the patriarch Jacob, [[1:17|those that possessed them|eos qui se possederant]], that is, all the nations which at one time harassed and subjugated the people of Israel. This is to be understood of spiritual dominion, not of temporal rule. For then the Apostles were made [[Ps 44:17|princes over all the earth|principes super omnem terram]]; and [[Ps 46:10|the strong gods of the earth are exceedingly exalted|dii fortes terræ elevati sunt vehementer]].

paras.t: Et erit domus Jacob ignis, et domus Joseph flamma, id est, Apostoli ceterique discipuli Christi ex duodecim tribubus Israel nati, igniti fuerunt et igne valde, ita ut ignis vocentur, quia et Spiritum Sanctum in igneis linguis receperunt. Et domus Esau erit stipula, id est, per prædicationem Apostolorum, corda Idumæorum igne Spiritus Sancti inflammabuntur cito et efficaciter, fidem et caritatem Christi recipiendo. Ideo sequitur: et succendetur in eis, id est, populus Idumææ per filios Jacob igne Sancti Spiritus succendetur; et devorabunt eos, id est, Idumæos consument quantum ad esse peccati, et Christo eos incorporabunt. Et non erunt reliquiæ domus Esau, id est, tales non remanebunt quales fuerunt, quemadmodum in Proverbiorum libro legitur: Verte impios, et non erunt. Expositio ista satis faciliter calumniari posset. Non enim universi conversi sunt Idumæi. Et sensus iste evidenter ad mysticum intellectum festinat.
paras.en: [[1:18|And the house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame|Et erit domus Jacob ignis, et domus Joseph flamma]], that is, the Apostles and the other disciples of Christ, born of the twelve tribes of Israel, were fiery and greatly aflame, so that they may be called fire, since they also received the Holy Ghost in fiery tongues. [[1:18|and the house of Esau stubble|Et domus Esau erit stipula]], that is, through the preaching of the Apostles the hearts of the Idumeans shall be set alight quickly and effectually by the fire of the Holy Ghost, receiving the faith and charity of Christ. Therefore there follows: [[1:18|and they shall be kindled in them|et succendetur in eis]], that is, the people of Idumea shall be kindled with the fire of the Holy Ghost through the sons of Jacob; [[1:18|and shall devour them|et devorabunt eos]], that is, they shall consume the Idumeans as regards the being of sin, and incorporate them into Christ. [[1:18|and there shall be no remains of the house of Esau|Et non erunt reliquiæ domus Esau]], that is, they shall not remain such as they were, as we read in the book of Proverbs: [[Prov 12:7|Turn the wicked, and they shall not be|Verte impios, et non erunt]]. This exposition could quite easily be attacked, for not all the Idumeans were converted. And this sense plainly hastens on to the mystical understanding.

paras.t: Potest ergo litteralius hoc modo exponi, quod præmemorati filii Jacob et domus Joseph, dicti sunt ignis, propter virtutem sententiæ excommunicationis, quam in adversarios veritatis ac fidei exercere valebant, imo et rebelles poterant tradere Satanæ in interitum carnis. In Apocalypsi quoque de duobus Christi testibus scriptum est, quod de ore ipsorum exivit ignis in adversarios eorum. Domus autem Esau sunt stipula, quia prædictæ sententiæ resistere non potuerunt, sed protinus latæ sententiæ percussæ sunt fulmine: quod de rebellibus est sumendum. Possunt autem per Idumæos intelligi cuncti gentiles: imo, secundum Hebræos et Hieronymum in primo suo prologo super istum Prophetam, quoniam Esau persecutus est fratrem suum Jacob, et Idumæi filii Esau Israelitas filios Jacob, propterea omnes adversarii Judæorum communiter nomine Edom designantur. Unde Judæorum doctores, qui post Christi passionem fuerunt et increduli permanserunt, per Edom quasi semper intelligunt Romam, et per Idumæos Romanos, a quibus finaliter destructum est dominium Judæorum, captivitasque gravissima introducta. Et devorabunt eos, id est, Apostoli præfatos rebelles damnationi fecerunt, vel potius ostenderunt, obnoxios, imo apostolica auctoritate condemnare poterant eos. Quod utique Apostoli maxime facient in die judicii, quando sedebunt in duodecim soliis Christo assidentes et conjudicantes.
paras.en: It can therefore be expounded more literally in this way: the aforesaid sons of Jacob and house of Joseph are called fire because of the power of the sentence of excommunication, which they were able to exercise against the adversaries of the truth and of the faith; indeed they could even [[1 Cor 5:5|deliver|tradere]] the rebellious [[1 Cor 5:5|to Satan for the destruction of the flesh|Satanæ in interitum carnis]]. In the Apocalypse too it is written of the two witnesses of Christ that [[Apoc 11:5|fire shall come out of their mouths|de ore ipsorum exivit ignis]] against their adversaries. And the house of Esau is stubble, because they could not withstand that sentence, but were at once struck by the thunderbolt of the sentence passed: which is to be taken of the rebellious. By the Idumeans, moreover, all the Gentiles may be understood: indeed, according to the Hebrews, and to Jerome in his first prologue on this Prophet, since Esau persecuted his brother Jacob[[Gen 27:41||]], and the Idumeans, the sons of Esau, persecuted the Israelites, the sons of Jacob, all the adversaries of the Jews are commonly designated by the name of Edom. Hence the doctors of the Jews who lived after the passion of Christ and remained unbelieving almost always understand Rome by Edom, and the Romans by the Idumeans, by whom the dominion of the Jews was finally destroyed and a most grievous captivity brought upon them. [[1:18|and shall devour them|Et devorabunt eos]], that is, the Apostles made the aforesaid rebels liable to damnation, or rather showed them to be so; indeed by apostolic authority they could condemn them. And this the Apostles will do above all on the day of judgment, when they shall sit on twelve thrones[[Matt 19:28||]], sitting beside Christ and judging with him.

paras.t: Et hereditabunt hi qui ad austrum sunt, id est Apostoli et cooperatores eorum ex Judaismo conversi, et in parte australi Judææ conversati, montem Esau et Philistiim; et possidebunt regionem Ephraim et Samariæ. Per hoc aliud nihil designatur, nisi quod Apostoli et adjutores eorum, populos terrarum istarum converterent, et fidei subderent, sempiternosque obedientiæ facerent filios. Et Benjamin possidebit Galaad. Paulus apostolus de tribu Benjamin ortus est, multosque convertit de consanguineis suis, qui simul cum eo evangelizaverunt. Unde in epistolis suis sæpe efficit mentionem de suis cognatis, quorum et nomina exprimit.
paras.en: [[1:19|And they that are toward the south, shall inherit|Et hereditabunt hi qui ad austrum sunt]], that is, the Apostles and their fellow workers, converted from Judaism and living in the southern part of Judea, [[1:19|the mount of Esau|montem Esau]] and [[1:19|the Philistines|Philistiim]]; [[1:19|and they shall possess the country of Ephraim|et possidebunt regionem Ephraim]] and [[1:19|the country of Samaria|Samariæ]]. By this nothing else is signified than that the Apostles and their helpers would convert the peoples of those lands and subject them to the faith, and make them everlasting sons of obedience. [[1:19|and Benjamin shall possess Galaad|Et Benjamin possidebit Galaad]]. The apostle Paul was born of the tribe of Benjamin[[Phil 3:5||]], and converted many of his kinsfolk, who preached the Gospel together with him. Hence in his epistles he often makes mention of his kinsmen, and gives their names too[[Rom 9:3||]][[Rom 16:7||]][[Rom 16:11||]][[Rom 16:21||]].

paras.t: Et transmigratio exercitus hujus filiorum Israel, id est fideles Israelitæ primitivæ Ecclesiæ, quos Christus transmigrare fecit de terra Judææ, dicendo: Euntes in mundum universum, prædicate Evangelium omni creaturæ; et eritis mihi testes usque ad ultimum terræ. De quibus et per Isaiam loquitur: Mittam ex eis qui salvati fuerint, ad gentes, in mare, in Africam et Lydiam, in Græciam et Italiam, ad insulas longe; et annuntiabunt gloriam meam gentibus. Possidebunt omnia loca Chananæorum usque ad Sareptam et ultra, id est, harum terrarum habitatores, fecerunt suos discipulos et Christi ministros, ita quod spiritualiter eis præsidebant.
paras.en: [[1:20|And the captivity of this host of the children of Israel|Et transmigratio exercitus hujus filiorum Israel]], that is, the faithful Israelites of the primitive Church, whom Christ made to go out from the land of Judea, saying: [[Mark 16:15|Go ye into the whole world and preach the gospel to every creature|Euntes in mundum universum, prædicate Evangelium omni creaturæ]]; and [[Acts 1:8|you shall be witnesses unto me|eritis mihi testes]] [[Acts 1:8|even to the uttermost part of the earth|usque ad ultimum terræ]]. Of them too he speaks through Isaias: [[Is 66:19|I will send of them that shall be saved, to the Gentiles into the sea, into Africa, and Lydia|Mittam ex eis qui salvati fuerint, ad gentes, in mare, in Africam et Lydiam]], [[Is 66:19|into Italy, and Greece, to the islands afar off|in Græciam et Italiam, ad insulas longe]]; [[Is 66:19|And they shall declare my glory to the Gentiles|et annuntiabunt gloriam meam gentibus]]. They shall possess [[1:20|all the places of the Chanaanites even to Sarepta|omnia loca Chananæorum usque ad Sareptam]] and beyond: that is, they made the inhabitants of these lands their disciples and ministers of Christ, so that they presided over them spiritually.

paras.t: Et ascendent salvatores, id est Apostoli instrumentaliter Christo cooperantes in conversione electorum, in montem Sion: ibi enim frequenter convenerunt ad tractandum de necessariis statum Ecclesiæ concernentibus; judicare montem Esau, id est discernere gentilitatem judicio discretionis, ad providendum eisdem: quemadmodum in Actibus fecisse leguntur, quando et conversis scripserunt gentilibus per manum Pauli ac Barnabæ, cum quibus miserunt Judam, Barsabam atque Silam viros primos in fratribus et prophetas, verbo dicentes: Visum est Spiritui Sancto et nobis, nihil imponere vobis oneris, quam ut abstineatis ab immolatis simulacrorum, et sanguine, et suffocato, et fornicatione. Et erit Domino Christo regnum militantis Ecclesiæ ubique terrarum, ita quod omnis tribus, gens, et linguæ servient ei, juxta illud in Psalmo: Adorabunt in conspectu ejus universæ familiæ gentium: quoniam Domini est regnum, et ipse dominabitur gentium. Et in Isaia: Multiplicabitur ejus imperium, et pacis non erit finis. De quo et Jeremias locutus est: Regnabit rex et sapiens erit. Postremo, nomine regni intelligi potest vel ipse populus subjectus seu subditi, vel gubernatio eorumdem. Solet quoque per regnum Domini, designari regnum Christi.
paras.en: [[1:21|And saviours shall come up|Et ascendent salvatores]], that is, the Apostles, working with Christ as his instruments in the conversion of the elect, [[1:21|into mount Sion|in montem Sion]]: for there they often assembled to deal with the necessary matters concerning the state of the Church; [[1:21|to judge the mount of Esau|judicare montem Esau]], that is, to discern the Gentile world with the judgment of discretion, so as to provide for them: as we read in the Acts that they did, when they wrote to the converted Gentiles by the hand of Paul and Barnabas, with whom they sent Judas, Barsabas and Silas[[Acts 15:22||]] [in Acts Judas and Barsabas are one man, Judas surnamed Barsabas], [[Acts 15:22|chief men among the brethren|viros primos in fratribus]], and prophets, saying in so many words: [[Acts 15:28|it hath seemed good to the Holy Ghost and to us to lay no further burden upon you|Visum est Spiritui Sancto et nobis, nihil imponere vobis oneris]], than that [[Acts 15:29|you abstain from things sacrificed to idols and from blood and from things strangled and from fornication|abstineatis ab immolatis simulacrorum, et sanguine, et suffocato, et fornicatione]]. [[1:21|and the kingdom shall be for the Lord|Et erit Domino Christo regnum]]: for the Lord Christ shall be the kingdom of the Church militant everywhere on earth, so that [[Dan 7:14|all peoples, tribes, and tongues shall serve him|omnis tribus, gens, et linguæ servient ei]], according to the words of the Psalm: [[Ps 21:28|And all the kindreds of the Gentiles shall adore in his sight|Adorabunt in conspectu ejus universæ familiæ gentium]]: [[Ps 21:29|For the kingdom is the Lord's; and he shall have dominion over the nations|quoniam Domini est regnum, et ipse dominabitur gentium]]. And in Isaias: [[Is 9:7|His empire shall be multiplied, and there shall be no end of peace|Multiplicabitur ejus imperium, et pacis non erit finis]]. Of whom Jeremias too spoke: [[Jer 23:5|a king shall reign, and shall be wise|Regnabit rex et sapiens erit]]. Lastly, by the name of kingdom may be understood either the subject people themselves, that is, the subjects, or the government of them. And by the kingdom of the Lord the kingdom of Christ is commonly meant.

paras.t: Hæc autem secunda loci istius expositio, consonat his quæ in ultimis capitulis Joelis ac Amos exposita sunt.
paras.en: This second exposition of the passage agrees with what has been expounded in the last chapters of Joel and Amos[[Joel 2:32||]][[Joel 3:21||]][[Amos 9:11||]].
